description: config.v2 §2.5, §2.10, §2.13, §2.18: one request against the test contract `contracts/rfcfg.v1.toml` and an owner's state -> accepted, or the refusal the owner sends, before any act. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked, never blessed. A case gives op (set, confirm, cancel, extend, persist), group (set's, the {g} of set/{g}), the request as `fields`, the JSON reading of its type (Set<T> for a set, Control otherwise; null where only bytes can say it), `hex`, the query's payload (core §7.5: CH, form 2, run width 0, the type's tag, then the record), and `state`: revision; pending, null or {token, applied: whether every group of the change is applied, deadline_passed: whether its deadline has come and its undo not yet run}; last, null or {token, set_sensitive}; persist, whether the owner has a persisted layer; in_flight, whether an act is in flight; writable, the groups the startup allowlist lets a set reach. Rows that need more state (an idempotency key held, the event's rate, a reach join near its deadline, the device) are lifecycle.json's. The order: persist without a layer, unavailable cause config, before the request is read; then a query under another Encoding (`encoding`, where a case gives it, zenoh/bytes where it gives none) is invalid_request, its bytes never read (core §5.1, "The request"; text 0.4); then a payload that does not parse as the request (core §7.5's refusals for a query, then §7.6's for the type: a value outside its bounds is an unused code) is invalid_request; then config.v1's rows without rows 3, 8 and 11. expect is {accepted: true}, or {refused: {code, cause, app}, reply_err}: code is core §5.2's, cause unavailable's alone, app the Error code app's alone, and reply_err the error form the owner sends (core §7.5, form 3) under `stamp`, the as-of mark the cases share, with Error's tag `error_tag`, no message and no detail. `desired`: a DesiredConfig (config.v1 §3) against the test contract and an allowlist -> {accepted: true} or {refused: {code, group, parameter}}: its revision above 4294967295 first (invalid_request, no group), then config.v1 §2.18's order, groups in the byte order of their names, each group's checks (not_found, contract, reach, unavailable), then each parameter in the byte order of its name (not_found, sensitive, invalid_request: not of its kind, a JSON integer with no fraction or exponent for an int, true or false for a bool, or outside its bounds). A group or parameter the contract does not declare is named null in the refusal, since the record carries indices.
